[Uncle Roger] What is the best value one of these things that would play the old Pokemon games?
[TheDukeOfNukem] Buy an R36S (or one of it's many clones) … I picked up another one, a K36, for 15 and change on Ali the other day while buying other stuff. For the price, nothing comes close. NES/SNES/N64, Mega Drive, Master System, all that old stuff. All the way up to PS1 is flawless (inc. GB/C/A). Can also do Dreamcast and NDS pretty much perfect. PSP is a bit more hit and miss, but plays a lot of them. And there's well into the four digits worth of games ported via the community and "PortMaster" from other consoles, PC, and phones, including 1:1 flawless native ports of stuff like GTA 3/VC/SA/LCS/CTW, Half Life, Simpsons Hit & Run, Postal, Quake 1,2,3, Duke Nukem 3D, and many many more.

[LilSlip] Which gen do you want to play?
I'm going to make some assumptions here- You're looking for good value, but also an authentic experience. Ex: you want to play dual screen games on a device that has dual screens, or you want to play the classics like Pokemon Red or Crystal on devices that feel like what you actually would have played them on ~20 years ago.
This means I'm excluding options like the Retroid pocket 4,5,6 as well as the flip 2, among others.
For the Gameboy and Gameboy advance games, there's a whole host of options. I'll quickly run through them:
Budget:
- R36 (cheapest 'good' handheld, beware of clones)
- RG35XX, 34XX and their respective SP versions (you can find these cheaper cause they're a bit older, SP one is clamshell like the GameBoy advance SP)
Mid-to-higher-tier:
- RG SP (slightly more expensive as handhelds listed before, but the best GBA SP clone)
- Konkr Pocket Advance (More expensive but more performant than the ones listed so far. Beware though- the company that sells this has really long shipping and customer support times. I know because I tried for a week to change my order's colour without success.)
- RG Rotate (the fun option, is more performant but you can't use that performance because of its form factor)
- Retroid pocket classic (At the discounted 99 dollar price, this is the device with the best build quality and screen you can get to play Game boy and Game Boy advance on)
If you want to play DS games, like Diamond, Pearl or Platinum:
Budget:
- RG DS (can be found for 100 AUD pretty reliably, but needs a lot of setup)
- RG DS Plus (Newer version with same performance and less setup required, as well as a better build, but as its new there haven't been signifcant discounts)
Mid-to-high tier:
- Retroid Pocket Duo Lite (non plus- can be had for 139 USD plus shipping, you get upscaled DS and android benefits with a decently faster processor compared to the RG DS)
If you want to play 3DS games as well:
Budget:
- No real good budget options exist. You could buy a tablet and run dual screen 3DS on it but if you're looking for an authentic experience you have to step up to the mid tier.
Mid-to-high tier:
- The duo lite mentioned before will just barely run 3DS, but it will not be that good of an experience.
- This Duo Lite Plus device is the cheapest 'great' entry point- same body as Duo Lite but faster processor.
High tier:
- Thor lite- Slightly slower processor, but smaller and better driver support for said processor. Will handle 3DS fine, do a little bit of switch.
- RP Duo- Slightly faster processor, better screens than Duo Lite or even the Thor, right now cheaper than the Thor base. Almost a no brainer- but the joystick is at the bottom (Playstation controller style) compared to the Thor having it at the top (Xbox style).
And if you want to play the latest Switch pokemon games (that also plays all the other generations) then there's still only one option- the Thor Base (or its higher tier options like the Pro and the Max).
Some other honourable mentions:
A10 mini for the smallest EDC Gameboy.
The aforementioned retroid pocket's as they're great power for the price, just probably not the right form factor for you.
Ayaneo Pocket Micro/Antec core Micro- great GBA but not worth its price arguably.
Your phone with a Pocket Taco (really small phone controller).
